A race official tries to stop Kathrine Switzer from becoming the first woman to run the official Boston Marathon. 1967.

In 1967, Kathrine Switzer became the first woman to run the official Boston marathon. At the time woman were not allowed in the race and Switzer was issued a number through an "oversight" in the entry screening process. When race official Jock Semple realized the error he attempted to physically remove her from the race. Switzer claims he shouted, "Get the hell out of my race and give me those numbers." Switzer's boyfriend Tom Miller, who was running with her, shoved Semple aside, allowing her to proceed.

The rules were subsequently changed and women officially allowed to compete after Semple oversaw implementation of qualifying times in 1970 and the formal admission of female runners in 1972.

Switzer later became the women's winner of the 1974 New York City Marathon, with a time of 3:07:29 (59th overall) and her personal best time iss 2:51:37, at Boston in 1975. Switzer was named Female Runner of the Decade by Runner’s World Magazine.

Last season, I feel like the political map worked handsomely, of course theres a few things that I learned and few changes that might be useful to implement especially with savagery. Please let me know what you think espeically with savagery point assignment, because they are mostly arbitrary. They might even be too technical or not technical enough, so let me know.

Castles, Forts:

* Castles and Forts take 3 savagery to create by a race. * They have a intrinsic defense Savagery of 2* its base savagery (only factors into getting attacked). * Cannot participate in trade

Towers, Outpost

* Towers cost 3 savagery to establish. * Their benefit is being able to watch. Any hero or race trying to move through a tile with a tower has a 80% chance of discovery * They can also provide 1+ Tech or 1+ Magic advantage to anyone operating inside one.

Cities

* Cities cost 5 savagery to establish. They build up by 2 savagery every sabbath. * Looting/Razing cities decreases savagery by 1/2. * Cities can trade

Territory/ Influence Zones

* Cost 2 Savagery per tile to claim (colonize). * Necessary to be established before building anything inside them. * Any hero or race moving through a influence zone has a 20% per tile chance of being discovered. If discovered, races have a chance to act on said hero or race. * A race discovering someone outside of their influence zone is considered highly unlikely, unless that party is okay with it.

Trade Routes:

* Trade Routes take 1 Savagery per tile to establish. * Trade routes are necessary to move any significant amount of some material from one place to another. * Trades provide an additional 1 savagery of growth to any city connected to it every sabbath.

Additional Notes for discussion: Armies still need to get figured out? Overlapping locations such as a castle with a city around it? How large should tiles be?
